title: Interview your analysts so data agents answer correctly
summary: A consultant open-sourced agent skills that interview analysts, write business context files and test answers; he reports accuracy rising from 87% to 95% on a fictional company.
agent_role: The agent interviews analysts domain by domain using query logs, writes context notes and test questions, and runs before-and-after checks. For business users, it drafts a plain plan for approval, runs it, and rates its own uncertainty.
outcome: Author reports accuracy rising from 87% to 95% on an imaginary demo company.
what_they_did: A data consultant turned his interview process into agent skills. The agent interviews a company's analysts one topic at a time, guided by past database queries. It saves what it learns as short text files in a shared folder on GitHub, and writes test questions along the way.
how_it_went: He reports that adding the context raised answer accuracy from 87% to 95% on a made-up open-source company called Shorelane.
worth_knowing: The gain was measured on a fictional demo company, not a real client. The author stresses keeping only context that changes answers, not repeating what other sources already hold.
prompt: Interview me about how our [business area] data works, one topic at a time. Use [our query logs or database] to guide your questions. Write what you learn as short notes in [a shared folder], and draft test questions with known answers from [our dashboards]. Then answer the test questions with and without the notes, and show me the difference. When I ask a business question later, write a plain plan for me to approve before running any queries.

curation.rationale: An open-source workflow where an agent interviews analysts to build business context and tests its value, with a reported accuracy gain, though only on a fictional demo company.
